description: Recursion shapes other than fib (mutual, Ackermann, tree build and walk, backtracking, merge sort, many-argument defaults, method recursion), at depths of up to about 700 frames.
notes: Maximum depth is about 700 frames instead of a few thousand: Bellard qjs's default stack overflows at about 1,550 frames of one-argument mutual recursion, about 1,200 with seven default parameters and about 1,500 for method recursion (zipp and node pass 3,000).

description: Generators, the iteration protocol and built-in iterables end to end, including early-exit cleanup counted into the checksum.
notes: Recursive yield* tree depth is kept at 10: Bellard qjs overflows at about 650 nested yield* levels.

description: Non-exceptional try/finally exits, labelled jumps, switch dispatch and a small share of Error construction with rethrow a few levels up.
A 100,000-record long-lived table and 512 old bucket arrays continuously receive freshly allocated objects, arrays and strings, mixed with non-escaping garbage.
notes: Peak working set, measured once: m node 114 MB, zipp 247 MB, qjs 89 MB; l node 234 MB, zipp 830 MB, qjs 146 MB.

description: An LRU cache of up to 50,000 string-keyed entries under steady insert/evict churn, with a retained survivor cohort and periodic bulk frees; the large size is an extended run.
notes: Peak working set, measured once: m node 138 MB, zipp 199 MB, qjs 47 MB; l node 357 MB, zipp 352 MB, qjs 45 MB.

description: Async functions awaiting async functions in depth and breadth, with Promise combinators, thenables and caught rejections, all completed on the microtask queue.
notes: The microtask-order hash (line 3) is the same on zipp and qjs as on node, so all three schedule await, thenable adoption and async return of a promise with the same tick counts.

description: Run-time compilation after warm-up: thousands of small distinct new Function and indirect-eval bodies, one large generated function, and direct eval of short expressions in a function scope.
notes: node may serve the repeated direct-eval sources from its eval cache. zipp's peak working set grows about 1.4 KB per dropped new Function, about the same as when every function is kept live, even under old-space allocation pressure (m 136 MB, l 594 MB; qjs 9 MB).
